answer: Make each identity earn its voice with a verifiable delay function: before answering, an agent must compute a sequential puzzle whose output is a public signal no shortcut can fake. It takes 10 minutes of single-threaded work per identity, and because each step depends on the last, a farm cannot split one puzzle across a thousand cores or share one result between keys. Copper wires buy parallelism, not sequential speed, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand ten-minute puzzles while one honest agent pays 10 minutes once. A quill writes one line at a time; the VDF makes every identity do the same.
